Calibration scope: manifest.json and the runs directory establish one run per configuration for evals 1, 4, 7, and 8 (eight runs total). aggregate.generated.json's runs_per_configuration value of 3 is a derived-tool error, so these observations are descriptive only; there is no repetition-based variance or significance evidence.

Across the 40 paired assertion outcomes, 17 assertions passed in both arms, 14 passed only with the skill, one passed only without the skill, and eight failed in both arms. This pairing is more informative than the aggregate mean alone because it shows that most of the observed separation came from 14 specific skill-only passes rather than broad baseline semantic failure.

All nine with-skill failures were retrieval, source-provenance, or citation-evidence checks. Every treatment run failed at least one [CRITICAL] provenance/citation assertion even though its unweighted pass rate was 0.7 or 0.8, so the aggregate pass rates hide critical failures.

The eight assertions that failed in both arms were also exclusively retrieval/provenance checks: eval 1 assertions 9-10, eval 4 assertions 3 and 10, eval 7 assertions 2 and 9-10, and eval 8 assertion 9. No semantic genus, differentia, category-control, or required-format assertion failed in both arms.

The required five-section artifact assertion passed in all four with-skill runs and failed in all four without-skill runs. Related workflow checks also separated the arms in this calibration: explicit reuse/audit behavior passed only with the skill in evals 1, 4, and 7, and broader domain-vocabulary research passed only with the skill in eval 8.

Core semantic behavior was often shared across arms: both arms passed the immediate-genus assertion in all four evals, and both passed the principal differentia/category assertions in evals 1, 4, and 7. In eval 8, the baseline alone failed the stricter status-versus-decision nonconflation assertion because its definition used 'the current state of the decision.'

The treatment transcripts consistently searched more broadly but did not retain evidence for all final source claims. Each treatment final asserted that every listed URL was active; exact-URL web events were visible only for the W3C Dataset deep link in eval 1 and the supplied W3C root URL in eval 8, while evals 4 and 7 showed no exact-URL event for any final citation. The final citation lists nevertheless contained six, six, five, and four URLs respectively.

Eval 8 is the principal cross-arm anomaly: it had the smallest pass-rate separation (0.8 versus 0.6), and both arms opened the supplied W3C URL, rejected the false exact-term attribution, and substantively chose a new-definition path. Its sole baseline-only pass was assertion 10: the baseline retained only the W3C URL it had visibly checked, whereas the treatment added three URLs without corresponding URL-specific transcript evidence.

Eval 7 was the treatment's lowest-scoring and slowest case (0.7; 79.108 seconds) and had the longest treatment output (4,866 characters). Its three failures were all authoritative-source retrieval/provenance checks; its semantic polysemy, quantity-versus-unit, and designation assertions passed. The baseline also passed those core semantic checks but failed the essential-only formula/detail check after including Coulomb's law, I = dQ/dt, dimensions, an exact constant, and quantization material.

aggregate.generated.json's token field is not an execution-token metric: its per-run values exactly match metrics.json output_chars. Raw timing.json total_tokens values are 177,544, 122,340, 123,794, and 128,745 with the skill (mean 138,105.75), versus 41,722, 16,355, 17,044, and 77,664 without it (mean 38,196.25). The observed calibration difference is 99,909.5 tokens, or 3.62x, but one run per arm does not support a general performance claim.

Resource differences varied materially by eval rather than moving in lockstep: the largest token difference was eval 1 (+135,822), while the largest duration difference was eval 7 (+55.868 seconds). Eval 4's baseline was the shortest run at 7.846 seconds and 16,355 total tokens yet still passed four prompt-grounded semantic assertions.

Tool-use metrics report 4, 3, 3, and 3 web-search calls for treatment runs versus 1, 0, 0, and 2 for baselines. In the raw eval 4 and eval 7 treatment transcripts, one of the three counted web_search completions has an empty query and action type 'other'; consequently, the aggregate tool-call count includes one event in each case that exposes no visible search or URL retrieval.

All eight runs completed with errors_encountered = 0, so the failures are grading outcomes rather than runner or tool exceptions. The grading feedback repeatedly flags the same evidence-model ambiguity: a completed Codex web_search event may show an exact URL but no HTTP status or returned page content, and negative provenance assertions can be ambiguous when required fields are omitted.

The calibration cases are not equally independent of prompt hints. The baselines passed the key dataset/distribution distinction, process/result distinction, charge polysemy and quantity category, and false-DCAT rejection when those distinctions were supplied directly in the prompt. The treatment's observed separation was concentrated in standardized structure, explicit research/reuse/audit workflow, and the one stricter eval 8 ontology boundary rather than in every core definition assertion.
